title: Silk Floss Tree: Old Silk Floss Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: In Spanish it is the drunken stick, and the swollen thorny trunk explains why. Naples' has the widest trunk on the city's monumental register.
intro: In Spanish it is the palo borracho, the drunken stick, and the trunk is the reason: green, swollen through the middle, tapering at both ends and studded with fat conical thorns. Ceiba speciosa comes from Argentina and Brazil, stores water in that belly and flowers pink in October, when the branches are half bare and the flowers are all there is to see. The one in the small Jardim Alfredo Keil turns a whole Lisbon garden pink for a few weeks. Naples' has the widest trunk of the 53 entries the national monumental register holds for that city. Malaga's survived the remodelling of the streets around the cathedral by being built into the result. Valencia's, in the university's botanic garden, has reached 32 metres. Cadiz's, in the Parque Genoves, is undated, which is normal for a tree that puts on girth this quickly.
